title: Faith and Truth - Episode 4: When Faith Feels Small

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome again to our SleepFit podcast series. This is Faith and Truth - Episode 4: When Faith Feels Small. It is your old friend again, Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Tonight, we're asking... what do we do when our faith feels too small to matter? <long pause>

In the gospel of Mark, a father brings his son to Jesus. <short pause> The boy has suffered terribly... thrown into fire and water by an evil spirit. <short pause> The disciples tried to help, but couldn't. <short pause> So the father comes to Jesus... and says something painfully honest. <long pause>
And ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us. <long pause>
Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth. <long pause>
And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: If you can do anything... have compassion on us, and help us. <short pause> There's such weariness in those words. <long pause>

This father has watched his child suffer for years. <short pause> He's seen failed attempts at healing. <short pause> He's desperate... but he's also cautious now. <short pause> If you can, he says. <long pause>
And Jesus responds to that... if. <short pause> If you can believe... all things are possible to him that believes. <long pause>
And immediately, the father cries out, with tears... <short pause> I believe. Help my unbelief. <long pause>

This is one of the most honest prayers in all of Scripture. <short pause> The man doesn't pretend his faith is strong. <short pause> He doesn't hide his doubt. <short pause> He simply brings both... belief and unbelief... to Jesus, at the same time. <short pause> And Jesus heals his son. <long pause>
Later, in Matthew's gospel, Jesus tells his disciples something that sounds almost impossible. <long pause>

And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Faith as small as a mustard seed. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: The mustard seed was the smallest seed a farmer would plant. <short pause> So Jesus is saying that the size of your faith isn't what matters most. <short pause> What matters is where you place it. <long pause>
A tiny seed of faith in the living God... can do what a mountain of confidence in yourself never could. <long pause>
The father in Mark didn't have great faith. <short pause> He had small, struggling, tear-stained faith. <short pause> But he brought it to Jesus. <short pause> That's the difference. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You don't have to feel strong tonight. <short pause> You don't have to muster up certainty, or convince yourself that everything will be fine. <short pause> Faith isn't a feeling you generate. <short pause> It's a turning toward someone who is faithful. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Maybe tonight, your prayer is simply... I believe. Help my unbelief. <short pause> Maybe you're tired of trying to force your way through something by sheer faith. <short pause> Maybe you've been disappointed before, and you're cautious now... like that father. <long pause>
Bring that to Jesus. <short pause> Bring the doubt. The weariness. The if you can. <short pause> He doesn't turn away honest hearts. <long pause>

The disciples asked Jesus why they couldn't heal the boy. <short pause> They'd been given authority... but something was missing. <short pause> And Jesus pointed them back to faith... even small faith... even mustard-seed faith. <long pause>
It's not about the strength of your grip on God. <short pause> It's about the strength of his grip on you. <long pause>

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: <exhales> You can rest in that tonight. <short pause> Your faith may feel fragile... but the one you're trusting is not. <short pause> He is able to do more than you can ask or imagine... and he doesn't require you to be strong first. <short pause> He meets you... where you are. <long pause>
Let's pray. <long pause> Lord, I believe... <short pause> help my unbelief. <short pause> Meet me in my smallness tonight... <short pause> and let me rest in your faithfulness. <long pause>
Goodnight.
